32	    matchEnd = matchStart + 1

content.text:
I fixed it: `[foo `bar` baz`` now renders as `

[foo bar baz`

`, and the image case `![alt `code` x`` renders the same way. I added both inputs as tests, and the markdown-it suite passes (205 tests, 0 failures). I didn't run the CommonMark spec tests, lint or type-check. **Cause:** When a `[` has no closing `]`, markdown-it scans to the end of the line looking for the label's end. That scan runs the backtick rule on the later backticks. In your example the final lone `` ` `` has no match, so the rule marks the whole line as "scanned, no closers found". It treats that as true for every opener, including the earlier `` `bar` `` that does have a closer. When the real parse reached `` `bar` ``, the cache said there was no closer, so it printed it as literal text. **Fix:** The "no closer found" cache now only applies to openers at or after the position where the failed scan began. Earlier openers fall back to a normal scan. The change is in `src/rules_inline/backticks.ts`, plus a new `backticksScanStart` field in `src/rules_inline/state_inline.ts`. The new tests are in `test/fixtures/markdown-it/commonmark_extras.txt`.
